Q: Python 3; How to display the contents of a CSV file, with rows filtered by the value in the timestamp column A:

In Python, pandas is a common package used for handling data. It can import data from CSV files and easily perform all the tasks you describe above. You can check out the user guide here: https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/user_guide/index.html . You do not NEED pandas to do what you described above, but it would give you a nice introduction to a fundamentally important package. The Python csv strategy given in the other answer would be a good way for you to learn some ins and outs of code, but could be painfully slow if your dataset is big.

After learning the basics, you can use read_csv() to turn your file into a DataFrame, which is a data structure pandas uses to store tabular data. The tutorials and documentation should help you figure out how to sort and print results. Ask for more help if you run into serious issues.

One note about #1: Unless your CSV file is truly massive, it will be read in pretty quickly. Displaying a loading screen is extra work that will slow the process down. I wouldn't recommend adding that in.

Q: How to execute a stored procedure against linked server? A:

I was able to get it to return a data from the IBMi/AS400 using the following syntax. It wasn't working prior to adding the {} in the stored procedure. It seemed to run but wouldn't return any data. I also set the library list on the linked server connection. If you don't do this, you will have to qualify the files in your stored procedure as well as the stored procedure call here.

EXEC ('{CALL IBMiStoredProcedureName (?)}', @PurchaseOrder) AT [LinkedServerName]

If you have multiple parameters, the syntax would be as follows.

EXEC ('{CALL IBMiStoredProcedureName (?,?)}', @PurchaseOrder, @POLine) AT [LinkedServerName]

Q: How to read XML into an ADODB.Stream object from the output of a SQL stored procedure that execs query FOR XML Auto A:

An example using MSOLEDBSQL19

sSQL = sSQL & "/*  QUERY  */" & vbCrLf

Dim cn As ADODB.Connection
Set cn = New ADODB.Connection
cn.CursorLocation = adUseServer
''https://www.w3schools.com/asp/prop_rec_mode.asp

'===== TEST CONNECTION EXECUTE =====

rst.Source = sSQL

'Display the data in the recordset.
While (Not rst.EOF)
   'sXMLResult = rst.Fields("AdditionalContactInfo").Value
   sXMLResult = rst.Fields(0).Value

CleanUp:
    On Error Resume Next
    'Application.EnableEvents = True
    If Not cn Is Nothing Then

Q: Is it possible to dynamically alter the constraints in MILP? A:

Yes, you can build the linear expression dynamically. Use sum().

In Sage MILP variables can be added together in a loop, so you do not need to write every term manually.

q.add_constraint(sum(v[k] for k in mini_keys) == 1)

That replaces both of your examples.

For example, if mini_keys has 9 entries, it creates:

v[mini_keys[0]] + ... + v[mini_keys[8]] == 1

If it has 6 entries, it creates:

v[mini_keys[0]] + ... + v[mini_keys[5]] == 1

So your constraint should simply be:

q.add_constraint(sum(v[key] for key in mini_keys) == 1)

If mini_keys can ever be empty, use Sage’s zero explicitly:

q.add_constraint(sum((v[key] for key in mini_keys), 0) == 1)

For multiple groups of keys, you can do the same in a loop:

for mini_keys in list_of_key_groups:
    q.add_constraint(sum(v[key] for key in mini_keys) == 1)

Q: Running a bat script with invoke-command works on vm:s but not on physical machines A:

As someone above said, it can be an issue with the WinRM memory quota. That post doesn't say what to do about that or how to tell if that's the issue.

This is straight from the AI and it resolved my issue: opatch.bat (and the direct java -jar call) launches the JVM with a fixed heap size, e.g. something like -Xmx... requested by OPatch. Under the WinRM remoting session, the process is subject to a much smaller memory/working-set limit than an interactive logon gets. By default, WinRM caps the memory available to remote shells (the MaxMemoryPerShellMB quota). When this happens inside opatch.bat, CMD's batch parser mangles the failed launch and reports the generic "The syntax of the command is incorrect."

This fix worked for me.

# Run this ON each target server (or via Invoke-Command) with admin rights.
Set-Item -Path WSMan:\localhost\Shell\MaxMemoryPerShellMB -Value 2048
Set-Item -Path WSMan:\localhost\Plugin\Microsoft.PowerShell\Quotas\MaxMemoryPerShellMB -Value 2048
Restart-Service WinRM

To set it remotely for the host you're testing:
powershell
Invoke-Command -ComputerName 'ServerName' -ScriptBlock {
    Set-Item WSMan:\localhost\Shell\MaxMemoryPerShellMB -Value 2048
    Set-Item WSMan:\localhost\Plugin\Microsoft.PowerShell\Quotas\MaxMemoryPerShellMB -Value 2048
    Restart-Service WinRM -Force
}
